description: Disciplined process hooks - hybrid prompt + Go binary approach

SessionStart.description: Initialize disciplined process, detect tracker, check MCP health

hooks.prompt: BLOCKING: Before committing, verify that all relevant tests pass. If you haven't run tests for the changes being committed, run them now. Do not proceed with the commit until tests pass. If there are no tests for the changed code, note this as a gap.

PreToolUse.description: Enforce spec-first workflow for implementation files

hooks.prompt: Check: Is this edit to an implementation file (not a test, spec, or doc)? If so, ensure a relevant [SPEC-XX.YY] reference exists in the codebase for the feature being modified. If you're implementing a new feature without a spec, suggest creating one first with /dp:spec. For bug fixes and minor changes, this check can be skipped.

PostToolUse.description: Validate spec trace markers after implementation edits
Validate spec trace markers after file writes

UserPromptSubmit.description: Analyze request for disciplined process phase and spec references

hooks.prompt: Analyze this request in the context of the disciplined process workflow. Consider: (1) What phase are we in? (orient/spec/decide/test/implement/review/close) (2) Does this request reference or require a spec? (3) Should an ADR be created for any architectural decision implied? (4) Are there task tracker items that should be updated? Silently incorporate these considerations into your response without explicitly mentioning this analysis unless relevant.

Before ending this session, check: (1) Are there uncommitted changes that should be committed? (2) Are there open task tracker items that should be updated or closed? (3) Has `bd sync --flush-only` been run? (4) Were any specs or ADRs modified that need review? Briefly mention any outstanding items to the user.
